fields.aka: Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura, Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Harivallabha (as a renunciant), Mahāmahopādhyāya
fields.appearance: 1576 Śaka (others: 1586), at Devagrāma (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna); the record: c. 1626-1664 according to scholars (Madhusūdana Tattvavācaspati: 1633-1638)
fields.disappearance: Māgha śukla pañcamī, at Rādhā-kuṇḍa (Abhidhāna; Gauḍīya calendar); year: 1708 (the record; the Sārārtha-darśinī finished in 1704); samādhi moved from Pātharpurā to the Gokulānanda temple
fields.place: Born at Devagrāma (Sāgardīghi, Murshidabad); studied at Saidābād; Rādhā-kuṇḍa and Vṛndāvana
fields.guru: Rādhāramaṇa Cakravartī (dīkṣā), son of Kṛṣṇacaraṇa Cakravartī, in Narottama Ṭhākura's line (Saṅkalpa-kalpadruma)
fields.disciples: Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa (who read the Bhāgavatam with him), Kṛṣṇadeva Sārvabhauma, Jagannātha Cakravartī (father of Narahari Cakravartī)
fields.notes:
Father: Rāmanārāyaṇa Cakravartī, a Rāḍhī brāhmaṇa; elder brothers Rāmabhadra and Raghunātha. Guru-praṇālī (Saṅkalpa-kalpadruma): Narottama → Gaṅgānārāyaṇa Cakravartī → Kṛṣṇacaraṇa Cakravartī (adopted son, his parama-guru) → Rādhāramaṇa Cakravartī (his dīkṣā-guru). Married young, left after one night spent telling his wife the Bhāgavatam; in Vṛndāvana leader of the Vaiṣṇavas; took veśa as Harivallabha (others: no veśa); installed Gokulānanda. Sent Baladeva with Kṛṣṇadeva Sārvabhauma to Galtā. Descendants at Bāluchar (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

The record had «Śrī Narottama dāsa Ṭhākura» as his guru: Narottama is the head of his line; his dīkṣā-guru was Rādhāramaṇa Cakravartī.

fields.aka: Baladeva Vidyābhūṣaṇa, Ekānti Govinda dāsa, Govinda dāsa
fields.place: Born near Remuṇā (Balasore, Orissa); Mysore; the Tattvavādī maṭha in Purī; Vṛndāvana (Śrī Śyāmasundara); Galtā near Jaipur (Śrī Vijaya-gopāla)
fields.guru: Rādhādāmodara of Kānyakubja (dīkṣā), a grand-disciple of Rasikānanda; studied the Bhāgavatam with Viśvanātha Cakravartī and bhakti-śāstra with Pītāmbara dāsa; earlier a Mādhva (Tattvavādī) sannyāsī
fields.works: Govinda-bhāṣya (on the Vedānta-sūtra); Siddhānta-ratna; Prameya-ratnāvalī; Vedānta-syamantaka; Siddhānta-darpaṇa; Aiśvarya-kādambinī; Sāhitya-kaumudī; Vaiṣṇavānandinī (on the Bhāgavatam); commentaries on the Gītā, the Ṣaṭ-sandarbha, the Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta, the Stava-mālā and others
fields.notes: Born near Remuṇā in Orissa; studied grammar, alaṅkāra and nyāya, went to Mysore for the Vedas and became a Mādhva; as a sannyāsī defeated the paṇḍitas of Purī and lived in the Tattvavādī maṭha; studied the Ṣaṭ-sandarbha with Rādhādāmodara and became his disciple; as a renunciant called Ekānti Govinda dāsa. Sent by Viśvanātha with Kṛṣṇadeva Sārvabhauma to Jaipur, he defeated the opponents at Galtā, installed Vijaya-gopāla and wrote the Govinda-bhāṣya by Govinda's order (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

fields.name: Śrī Narahari Cakravartī (Ghanaśyāma dāsa)
fields.aka: Narahari Cakravartī, Ghanaśyāma Cakravartī, Ghanaśyāma dāsa, Narahari dāsa, Narahari Dāsa Ghanaśyāma Dāsa, Rasuiyā Pūjārī
fields.notes:
Son of Jagannātha, a disciple of Viśvanātha Cakravartī; born at Reñāpur (Reñāgrām), Murshidabad (the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna: at the beginning of the 17th century). Unmarried until his parents died; then by Govindajī's order His cook in Vṛndāvana («Rasuiyā Pūjārī»). Cook, singer, musician and great devotee; wrote the lives of the ācāryas after Mahāprabhu (Bhakti-ratnākara, Narottama-vilāsa); the fifth and twelfth waves of the Bhakti-ratnākara map Vraja and Navadvīpa.

He had two names: Ghanaśyāma (also his signature in his songs) and Narahari — «Narahari dāsa Ghanaśyāma dāsa»; Ghanaśyāma Cakravartī #328 was the same person (merged 06-11-2026, Whisper). Not Ghanaśyāma Cakravartī of Budhuri, grandson of Govinda Kavirāja.

fields.name: Śrī Rādhāmohana Ṭhākura
fields.guru: Of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya's family (son of Jagadānanda Ṭhākura); his own guru not stated in the Abhidhāna
fields.disciples: Vaiṣṇava Caraṇa dāsa; Uddhava dāsa (padakartā); Vaiṣṇava dāsa (Gokulānanda Sena, compiler of the Padakalpataru); Kālindī dāsa; Parāṇa dāsa; Mahārāja Nandakumāra
fields.works: Padāmṛta-samudra, with its commentary Mahābhāva-anusāriṇī; 182 songs in the Padakalpataru
fields.notes:
A descendant of Śrīnivāsa Ācārya, of Mālihāṭī; a great paṇḍita and padakartā. Converted Mahārāja Nandakumāra; took part in the debate on svakīyā and parakīyā at Murshid Quli Khan's court (1125 BS). Passed away on Caitra śukla navamī in harināma-saṅkīrtana in the tulasī garden; his wife seven days later (Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).

The record had «Śrīnivāsa Ācārya» as his guru: he was of his family, born more than a century later.
